Action.description:
An action triggered by a key binding or a menu entry.

In YAML, actions without a parameter are plain strings (`close`) and
actions with one are single-key mappings (`workspace: 2`).

oneOf.description:
Start a program, given as a list: the program followed by its
arguments. No shell is involved, so nothing is expanded or split.
Ask the focused window to close.

Ask every window of the program the focused window is of to close,
as its close button would, so that the program may ask to save: as
Cmd+Q quits a program on a Mac. Its program is the windows that share
its application's name; one that has none is a program of its own.
Toggle the focused window between maximized and its normal size.
Toggle fullscreen for the focused window.
Hide the focused window.

Hide every window of the program the focused window is of, on any
workspace, as Cmd+H does on a Mac.

Hide every window of every program but the focused window's, as
Cmd+Option+H does on a Mac.

Set every window of the workspace shown aside, to show the desktop,
as a Mac does: each slid straight out from the middle of the screen
until a sliver is left at an edge, not minimized, and back where it
was once this is asked again, Escape is pressed, a window or its
sliver is chosen, or one opens, or as its workspace is left.
Roll the focused window up into its titlebar, or let it down again.
Keep the focused window above the others, or stop keeping it there.

Have the focused window on whichever workspace its screen is
showing, or leave it on the one it is on.
Focus the next window on the workspace.
Focus the previous window on the workspace.

Open the switcher at the window used before the one in use, or,
while it is open, go on to the next. Letting go of the keys held
with it chooses the window it is at.

The same, going back: the switcher opens at the window used longest
ago.

Open the switcher at the program used before the one in use, as
Cmd+Tab does: each program once, by its window used last; or, while
it is open, go on to the next. The program chosen comes forward with
all its windows on the workspace.

The same, going back: the switcher opens at the program used
longest ago.

Focus the next window of the focused window's program on its
workspace, going round, as Cmd+backquote does.

Focus the window of the focused window's program before it on its
workspace, going round.

Open the overview, every window of the workspace side by side
under the workspaces of the screen, to pick one from; or close it.

Open the overview with only the windows of the focused window's
program on its workspace, as a Mac's App Exposé shows them, to pick
one from; or close the overview, whichever windows it shows.
Switch to the tab after the active one in the focused window's group.
Switch to the tab before the active one in the focused window's group.

Have the focused window take a half of where it is: `left`,
`right`, `top` or `bottom`. The next window to open there has the
other half. From a desktop, where it is becomes a workspace made
for it.

Give focus to the window beside the focused one, among windows
that share a workspace: `left`, `right`, `up` or `down`.

Change the focused window over with what is beside it, among
windows that share a workspace: `left`, `right`, `up` or `down`.

Switch to the workspace with this number. One past the last makes
that workspace first.

Make a workspace after the last and switch to it. It goes again
once it is empty and another is shown.
Switch to the following workspace.
Switch to the preceding workspace.

Send the focused window to the workspace with this number, on the
screen it is on. One past the last makes that workspace first.
Send the focused window to a workspace made for it, after the last.

Put the focused window beside those that share a workspace made
for windows, known by the `id` the state gives it, and show that
workspace.
Send the focused window to the next screen.
Open the root menu at the pointer.
Open the launcher, to start a program by typing its name.

Give the notifications the keyboard, the newest first: Tab and the
arrow keys go through it and its buttons, Enter chooses, as a click
does, and Escape dismisses it.

Show the welcome card: a step at a time, what the keys that matter
do, light or dark, the wallpapers that come with omorfos, and the
applications that open what. It is shown by itself at the first
login.

Show "About omorfos": its version, and what it is made with that is
someone else's. Asked again while it is shown, it goes.
Lock the session, with the program `locker` in config.yaml names.
Put the machine to sleep, as `omorfos-session sleep` does.

Start the machine again, as `omorfos-session restart` does: once
the user has said so, unless `power.ask` in config.yaml is false.

Turn the machine off, as `omorfos-session shut-down` does: once the
user has said so, unless `power.ask` in config.yaml is false.

End the session, as `quit` does: once the user has said so, unless
`power.ask` in config.yaml is false.

Open the application the system has as the default for this, as
`mimeapps.list` says; or, with none, say so.

Keep the session from locking, the screens from going off and the
machine from sleeping when the user is away, until asked again; or,
while it is kept so, let it go.
The same for at most this many seconds, up to a day.

Make the screens warm now if they are not, as warm as `night_light`
says, or as they are if they are, until night light next turns them
by the time of day.

Type with the next of the keyboard's layouts, and after the last
with the first again.

Have the screens stand the next way: as the configuration says, all
showing what the first shows, and each alone. Each is kept only if
the user says so in time.

Guess anew the scale for every screen plugged in, in place of the
one guessed when each was first seen, and keep that from now on: as
a newer version of omorfos would guess. A scale `config.yaml` gives
is laid over it still.
The same for one screen, by its socket's name or one from `screens`.
Re-read the configuration now.

Start the compositor again, keeping the login, as `omorfos-hold`
does when it ends: the newest version installed. Programs stay open
through it, their windows where they were, but for programs written
for X11, which close with their X server.
End the session.

Application.description:
A kind of application the `open` action opens: whichever the system
has as the default for it.

oneOf.description: What opens web links (`x-scheme-handler/https`).
What opens folders (`inode/directory`).
What opens plain text (`text/plain`).

The terminal: the first that `xdg-terminals.list` names, as
`xdg-terminal-exec` reads it, or `foot` where none is named.
omorfos's settings, which are not there yet.

Binding.description: One key binding: the keys to press and what they do.

keys.description:
The keys to press, such as `Super+Return`. Separate several chords
with spaces to make a chain pressed one after another, such as
`Super+x t`.

Command.description: A program followed by its arguments, run without a shell.

oneOf.description: Whether the built-in bindings are kept: a Mac's, with Super for Command, if true; none if false.
`ordinary`: the ordinary way's, with Ctrl and Alt as Windows, GNOME and KDE have them.
The left half.
The right half.
The top half, or upwards.
The bottom half, or downwards.

KeyChain.description: Chords such as `Super+Return`, separated by spaces when chained.

Role.description:
Something a program may do only if the compositor started it and was
told it may.

oneOf.description:
Put surfaces on the screen outside windows and keep room for them,
and list the windows.
Cover the screen and take the keyboard while it does.
Lock the session.
Show the prompt that asks for a secret.
Take pictures of the screen and of windows.
Read and set the clipboard at any time.
Type and click as the user, and see what is typed into fields.
Arrange the screens and change their colour.

Started.description: A program to start with the session: its name and arguments, or that and what it may do.

may.description: What it may do that an ordinary program may not.

description: `keys.yaml` as written, before conflicts between bindings are checked.

bindings.description:
The key bindings, beside the built-in ones. One on keys a built-in
binding uses, or that begin with them, takes its place.

defaults.description:
Which built-in bindings are kept, on the keys these bindings leave
alone: a Mac's, with Super for Command, unless this is `ordinary`,
for the ordinary way's with Ctrl and Alt, or `false`, for none.

unbind.description: Built-in bindings to do without, by their keys, such as `Super+h`.
